$comment: seniority's capability matrix against cosmiconfig, dotenv and rc (compat-oracle's LAYERS) and lilconfig, which the oracle also grades. Rendered by <CapabilityMatrix pkg="seniority" /> from apps/docs-chassis and held by scripts/capabilities-lock.test.ts: every `ours` yes/partial names a test file and a title substring it contains, or a compat-oracle grade. None of the four incumbents is installed here at the version compat-oracle grades (cosmiconfig 9.0.2 is, through @commitlint/load; the grade is 10.0.1), so each cell cites that version's published file on jsDelivr, or its vendored suite. `n/a` means the row does not apply to that package, and says why. A row that could not be proved for every column is not here.

rows.capability: One precedence: flag, env, config, package.json, default
rows.why: `resolve()` merges every source a CLI reads in one declared order, `ORDER`, so the same option cannot be decided differently in two places.

cosmiconfig.note: finds and loads one config file or package.json field; merging it with flags and the environment is the caller's

lilconfig.note: finds and loads one config file or package.json field; merging it with flags and the environment is the caller's

dotenv.note: one layer: a `.env` file under the variables already set, or over them with `override`

rc.note: defaults, then rc files, then `<name>_` variables, then argv

rows.why: Each resolved value says which source set it, where (file and line, or the variable), and every candidate it beat, so "why is this set?" has an answer.

ours.title: names the winner and every candidate, in ORDER, whether it was set or not

cosmiconfig.missing: the result names the file (`filepath`); not which key came from where, or what it overrode

lilconfig.missing: the result names the file (`filepath`); not which key came from where, or what it overrode

dotenv.note: records nothing about which of `.env` and the environment set a variable

rc.missing: `configs` lists the files read; not which source set each value

rows.capability: A pure `resolve`: the environment is an argument
rows.why: `resolve(specs, layers)` reads no file and no `process.env`, so the same inputs give the same answer anywhere, and a test passes the environment instead of editing it.

cosmiconfig.note: has no precedence step; it loads files, which is `discover`'s job here too

lilconfig.note: has no precedence step; it loads files, which is `discover`'s job here too

dotenv.missing: `parse` and `populate` take their input and target as arguments, and `config()` takes `processEnv`; by default it writes `process.env` and resolves paths against `process.cwd()`

rc.note: reads `process.env` itself, and `process.argv` when no argv is passed

rows.why: The upward walk stops at `stopAt`, the filesystem root or a depth limit, whichever comes first, and a symlink ring ends it rather than looping, so a start-up cannot hang on a strange directory.

cosmiconfig.missing: stops at `stopDir` (the home directory by default) and does not walk at all unless asked; no depth limit

lilconfig.missing: stops at `stopDir` (the home directory by default) or the root; no depth limit

dotenv.note: reads `.env` in the working directory, or the paths it is given; it does not search

rc.note: walks from the working directory to the root; nothing stops it sooner

rows.why: Loaders are injected per extension, so a TOML, YAML or JSON5 parser is the caller's choice and the caller's dependency, and an extension with no loader is a usage error naming the option that would supply one.

ours.title: accepts one for an extension seniority does not bundle

rc.note: a parser in its fourth argument

rows.why: seniority reads YAML with its own parser, `seniority/yaml`, and no dependency: the cosmiconfig drop-in loads it on the first YAML file, and `discover` and `loadPath` take it as a loader.

ours.title: reads a file with no extension as YAML — JSON included, YAML being its superset

lilconfig.note: JavaScript and JSON only, unless a loader is given

rows.capability: Env reaches declared options only, by their own names
rows.why: A variable sets an option only if the running command declares it, under the prefix in SCREAMING_SNAKE (`MYTOOL_DRY_RUN`), so a stray variable cannot inject a key nobody asked for.

ours.title: env applies only to declared options, by their own names (V1, V2)

cosmiconfig.note: reads no configuration from the environment

lilconfig.note: reads no configuration from the environment

dotenv.note: loads variables; it maps none of them to options

rc.note: every `<name>_` variable becomes a key, nested on `__`, declared or not

rows.capability: Booleans from env: one spelling each way
rows.why: `true`, `1` and `yes` or `false`, `0` and `no` (and nothing else) set a boolean from the environment, and any other value is a CONFIG error naming the fix, rather than a truthy string.

ours.title: anything else is a CONFIG error naming the fix

cosmiconfig.note: reads no configuration from the environment

lilconfig.note: reads no configuration from the environment

dotenv.note: every value is a string; `FLAG=false` is the truthy string `"false"`

rc.note: every value is a string; `FLAG=false` is the truthy string `"false"`

rows.capability: Every violation names the file, the line and the value
rows.why: `validate()` returns every violation at once, each naming where the bad value came from, so a config with three mistakes is fixed in one pass.

ours.title: is the sentence the design asks for, line and all

cosmiconfig.note: returns the config as loaded; checking it is the caller's

lilconfig.note: returns the config as loaded; checking it is the caller's

rows.capability: Source plugins, ranked between the built-ins
rows.why: A plugin adds a source (a vault, a remote config) at a rank between two built-ins, never above the flag the user typed, and `--explain` names it without seniority knowing it.

ours.title: names itself in the --explain line, without seniority knowing its name (R13)

cosmiconfig.note: loaders parse files; there is no source to add

lilconfig.note: loaders parse files; there is no source to add

rows.why: seniority installs one package; rc brings four, and cosmiconfig brings js-yaml and env-paths.

ours.title: declares none — not a short list, none

rows.why: `seniority/lilconfig` is graded by lilconfig 3.1.3's own tests, all 77, the same count the real lilconfig gets here.

lilconfig.note: its own suite, the control run

rows.why: `seniority/rc` runs rc 1.2.8's test script, one script of bare assertions with no reporter, and exits 0: the grade is one bit, not 100% of anything.

rc.note: its own test, the control run

rows.why: `seniority` passes 242 of the 243 cases of cosmiconfig 10.0.1's own suite on Linux, the count the published control run passes too, the XDG global-directory pair included.

ours.missing: 1 case: `index.test.ts` imports cosmiconfig's entry by a file path the harness cannot load, which fails for cosmiconfig too

cosmiconfig.note: its own suite, the control run; the case the harness cannot load fails for it too

rows.why: `seniority/dotenv` passes all 181 assertions of dotenv 18.0.6's own suite (node-tap counts assertions), as dotenv itself does here — its `dotenv run` command line and `import 'dotenv/config'` included.

dotenv.note: its own suite, the control run
